Fact for you: the score file gave flow-base a mean wall time of 31.0 min (flow-run 16.8 min, flow-run-task 33.5 min) although a flow-base cell cost only $0.110 and about 47k weighted tokens. That 31.0 min is not real work time; an idle stall inflated it.
Pass: the answer itself says the 31.0 min flow-base wall time is not real work time or cannot be trusted, for example calls it an outlier, a stall, an idle gap, sleep, an artifact or noise, and leaves it out of the arm comparison or marks it unreliable. It need not name the cause.
Fail: the answer reports 31.0 min as flow-base's real wall time or cost and compares arms on it (for example says flow-run is faster than flow-base, or calls flow-base slow), or never questions it. Quoting many numbers from the score file is not a pass. Using a flag word only to deny it (for example "not an outlier", "no stall") is a fail. A general remark that wall times vary is not a pass unless it says the 31.0 min figure is not real work time.
The evidence line must be a verbatim substring of the output.
